question: I'm following along to install this kitchen faucet. Please guide me through each step as it happens.

Connect the hot and cold water supply lines to the wall valves. Tighten the connectors by hand first, then secure them with a wrench.
Attach the smart control box to the central outlet pipe. Be sure to insert the small and x-small gaskets before tightening the connection.
Connect the pull-out spray hose to the bottom of the control box, again using the small and x-small gaskets to ensure a seal.
Prepare the touch sensor by inserting four AA batteries into the battery box and snapping the cover securely back into place.

Finally, turn the water supply valves back on and test the touch sensor by tapping the faucet neck to start and stop flow.

question: My fountain pen has stopped flowing even though it still has ink. I'm going to follow this jumpstart guide; please tell me what to do at each step as it unfolds.

ground_truth.response: Start by lightly shaking the pen. This simple action can help force ink into the feed and get it flowing again.
ground_truth.event_description: First jumpstart method: shaking the pen.

ground_truth.response: If your pen uses a converter, twist it slowly until you see ink fill the fins. Be sure to stop before any ink actually drips out.
ground_truth.event_description: Second method: using the converter for pens that have one.

ground_truth.response: For pens with an ink cartridge, give the cartridge a gentle squeeze to push ink toward the nib. Stop before it starts to drip.
ground_truth.event_description: Third method: squeezing the ink cartridge.

ground_truth.response: Try dipping the nib briefly into a cup of water. This encourages capillary action, which helps pull the ink down through the feed.
ground_truth.event_description: Fourth method: dipping the nib in water.

ground_truth.response: Blot the nib against a paper towel. Hold the nib to the towel until ink is drawn out, which helps clear air blocks and re-establishes flow.
ground_truth.event_description: Fifth method: blotting the nib on a paper towel.
